edits.headline: US charges 17 people over $1.3m Social Security theft
edits.subheadline: One of them is a Chicago woman who kept her dead mother's body in a freezer, the New York Post reported.
editorialBody: The US Department of Justice on Tuesday 29 September charged 17 people with stealing more than $1.3m in Social Security benefits, the New York Post reported.
One of them is a Chicago woman who kept her dead mother's body in a freezer. She is accused of collecting her mother's retirement benefits, WJLA reported, citing the New York Post.
A US ban on imports of some Canadian alcohol, dairy products and motorcycles took effect on 29 September, DW News and CNBC reported.
The ban covers about $967m of Canadian imports in 2025, most of it alcohol, according to Jacob Jensen of the American Action Forum.
Iran's parliament speaker said that if Iran's oil sales and security are not guaranteed, "neither are anyone else's", Press TV reported.
A judge refused bail to anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas, who denies criminal damage over the alleged slashing of a migrant boat, BBC News reported.
Thomas was remanded in custody at Portsmouth Crown Court, and a provisional trial date was set for 1 March 2027, AFP reported.
